A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Partial Gromov Wasserstein Metric work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including distinguishing removed material from relocated sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original shape-matching, retrieval, interpolation, solver-runtime, and positive-unlabeled learning experiments, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original shape-matching, retrieval, interpolation, and solver-runtime results, including Table 1 and appendix figures.

M1.justification: v3 removes the complete PU-learning adaptation from v2 Appendix P, including the transport-marginal quantile classifier and proposed FLB-POT initialization. This removes a distinct application procedure. The core PGW objective, two Frank-Wolfe solvers, and barycenter algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The PU-learning evaluations on MNIST, EMNIST, and the Amazon, Webcam, and DSLR domains of Caltech Office disappear, including within-domain and cross-domain settings using SURF/DECAF features. The shape datasets, outlier scenarios, interpolation tasks, and synthetic timing coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The deleted PU study removes evaluated POT and FLB-UOT initialization alternatives to the proposed FLB-POT initializer, alongside its MPGW/UGW comparisons. Comparator membership in the retained shape and solver-runtime experiments is unchanged; newly cited related methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: v3 removes the distinct PU evaluation protocol, including its SCAR assumption, known positive proportion of 0.2, source/target sample budgets, and disabled line search. In retained shape retrieval, fixed SVM sigma = 10 becomes per-method selection from eight values spanning 0.001 to 10000. Stratified ten-fold evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Removing the PU appendix eliminates the comparisons of initialization accuracy, final accuracy, and runtime across POT, FLB-UOT, and FLB-POT, together with the embedding-separability visualization and analysis. The existing outlier-matching and noise-corrupted interpolation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10,000 repetitions of nearest-neighbor representative selection and mean SVM accuracy across ten folds. No changes to seed disclosure, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance testing are introduced; the removed PU results did not report these.

E6.justification: All PU accuracy and runtime entries in v2 Tables 2–5 are removed. In Table 1(a), MPGW accuracy changes from 0.0813 to 0.2375 on Dataset I and from 0.0000 to 0.2500 on Dataset II; UGW Dataset II changes from 0.7833 to 0.9000, overtaking GW. These accompany changed SVM tuning, rather than demonstrating same-setting gains. PGW accuracies and Table 1(b) runtimes are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix K substantially revises the Lipschitz-bound derivation, replacing the sqrt(nm)-scaled expression with an nm-scaled maximum bound and adding Lemmas K.1–K.2, Proposition K.3, and further remarks. Lemma E.2 gains explicit penalty thresholds. Proposition L.1 gains a fixed-mass equivalence and objective-value identity, followed by new non-equivalence examples in L.3–L.4. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and summary retain the same principal claims: a metric for non-probability mm-spaces, two equivalent Frank-Wolfe solvers, PGW barycenters, and effective shape applications. The new non-global-optimality footnote clarifies solver scope already reflected in v2's stationary-point convergence discussion.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies the solvers' non-global optimality and expands the interpretation of the PGW–MPGW relationship. It removes the specific warning that line search can terminate prematurely and harm PU performance. Although the standalone limitations appendix disappears, its MDS rotation/reflection ambiguity discussion remains in Appendix M.1.

D1.justification: Deleting the PU appendix removes substantial reproducibility information: autoencoder embedding dimensions, feature choices, initialization formulas, solver tolerances, iteration limits, numerical precision, sample sizes, and dataset access links. v3 documents the replacement SVM parameter grid. Hardware specifications and implementation details for retained experiments remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning robust partial-Wasserstein metrics and expands convergence comparisons with supervised GW in Remark K.7. PU-learning and associated dataset/feature references are removed. The central positioning against UGW and mass-constrained PGW, including the metric novelty claim, remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact, with local wording corrections and a clearer proof roadmap. Appendices K and L receive localized restructuring into named lemmas, propositions, examples, and remarks; point-cloud matching moves from M.2 to Appendix N. The PU section, standalone limitations section, and acknowledgments are removed without a wholesale reorganization of the remaining paper.

P2.justification: v3 removes the eight-panel PU dataset visualization in Figure 10 and all four PU results tables. Retained Figures 7 and 8 are reduced and placed together on one page, and the barycenter algorithm boxes are regrouped. Table 1 gains an overall caption. The retained experimental figure content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: Per-method SVM tuning addresses the earlier shared-parameter comparison, and the explicit non-global-optimality qualification improves clarity. However, v3 loses the PU evidence about applicability beyond shape tasks and its specific line-search failure disclosure. The revised theory is also not an unambiguous repair: Equation (71) bounds the minimum gap across iterations, while Proposition K.3 states a per-iteration bound without an additional argument. These benefits and unresolved weaknesses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
